physics_goals.quote: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) will measure the effect of dark energy on the expansion of the universe.
physics_goals.value: Measure the effect of dark energy on the expansion of the universe with a three-dimensional map of tens of millions of galaxies and quasars.

physics_goals.quote: DESI's principle scientific objectives are to place precise constraints on the equation of state of dark energy, the gravitationally driven growth of large-scale structure, and the sum of the neutrino masses
physics_goals.value: Constrain the dark-energy equation of state, the growth of large-scale structure and the sum of the neutrino masses, and explore signatures of primordial inflation.

summary.plain: A spectroscopic instrument on a 4-metre telescope in Arizona that records the light of up to 5,000 galaxies and quasars at once. Measuring how far away tens of millions of them are, it maps the universe in 3D to see how dark energy shapes cosmic expansion.
summary.technical: Stage IV dark-energy experiment: 5020 robotic fibre positioners feeding ten spectrographs (360–980 nm) at the prime focus of the 4-m Mayall telescope, Kitt Peak. Measures baryon acoustic oscillations and redshift-space distortions with galaxies, quasars and the Lyman-alpha forest. Main survey began 14 May 2021; the planned five-year survey was reported complete on 15 April 2026 and observations continue.

unique_capabilities.quote: DESI can obtain 5000 spectra per observation, has a 1000 s science exposure time in nominal conditions, and only requires approximately 2 min to change between fields.
unique_capabilities.value: A prime-focus corrector and 5020 robotic fibre positioners on a 0.812 m focal surface let DESI record about 5000 spectra per exposure, far more than the roughly 1000 per plate of eBOSS.
